section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch7 — Memory & Forgetting
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: After a sound has stopped, a brief auditory 'echo' of it lingers in the mind for a second or two, allowing a person to briefly recall the last few words of a sentence even if they were momentarily distracted while it was being spoken. This brief auditory sensory memory store is called:
explanation: Echoic memory is the brief auditory sensory register (lasting a few seconds), the auditory counterpart to iconic memory (the brief visual sensory register) — both part of Atkinson-Shiffrin's sensory memory stage, the first and shortest-lived stage of the multi-store memory model.
